description: Writes game_tags rows for a run, replacing any prior rows for that run (idempotent re-run, mirroring write_enriched).
signature: def write_tags(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, rows: Iterable[TagRow]) -> int
docstring:
Replace a run's tag rows.

Args:
    conn: An open connection.
    run_id: The run these tags belong to.
    rows: An iterable of TagRow. May contain multiple rows for the same appid (different tags) but not the same (appid, tag) pair twice.

Returns:
    The number of rows written.

Raises:
    StorageError: If run_id does not exist, or the same (appid, tag) pair appears twice in rows.
postconditions: All prior game_tags rows for run_id are replaced atomically
Every written row satisfies the (run_id, appid, tag) primary key uniqueness

edge_cases.input: The same (appid, tag) pair given twice with different vote counts
edge_cases.expected_behavior: StorageError, since this indicates a caller-side deduplication bug in extract_tags, not something storage should silently resolve

unit_tests.name: test_write_then_read_tags
unit_tests.description: Written rows are exactly readable back via read_tags.
unit_tests.expected: read_tags returns the same set of (appid, tag, votes, rank) tuples

unit_tests.name: test_duplicate_pair_raises
unit_tests.description: Two TagRow entries with the same (appid, tag) raise StorageError.

unit_tests.name: test_empty_iterable_writes_zero
unit_tests.description: No rows given writes zero and returns 0.
